t: An EAR policy with SI ₹100 crore in Zone II has EQ cover on first-loss basis at 10% of SI. If the tariff EQ premium for full SI would be ₹5 lakh, the EQ premium chargeable is
e: First-loss EQ: 10% of SI attracts 40% of the tariff EQ rate, i.e. 40% × ₹5 lakh = ₹2 lakh (20% of SI would attract 50%).

t: Loss of Rent cover: SI ₹12,000, term of rent insured 12 months, period of reinstatement 6 months, rent claimed ₹8,000. The amount payable after applying the economic limit and under-insurance is
e: Economic limit = SI × RI period/term = 12,000 × 6/12 = ₹6,000. Rent/month claimed = 8,000/6 = ₹1,333.33; sum to be insured = 1,333.33 × 12 = ₹16,000; under-insurance 8,000 × 12,000/16,000 = ₹6,000.

t: For a 250 MW combined-cycle gas-based power plant under EAR, the minimum deductible for a testing-period claim is
o: 10% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹50 lakh
5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹60 lakh
5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹125 lakh
5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹100 lakh
e: Combined-cycle/gas plants: 50–200 MW – min ₹60 lakh testing/₹20 lakh normal; 200–300 MW – ₹100 lakh/₹50 lakh; 300 MW and above – ₹125 lakh/₹75 lakh.

t: The obligatory cession that Indian general insurers must make to GIC Re is currently:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The obligatory cession was reduced to 4% from 1 April 2022.

t: The minimum paid-up equity capital required to start a life or general insurance company in India is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹100 crore for a direct insurer; ₹200 crore for a reinsurer (Section 6 of the Insurance Act).

t: Under the Agreed Bank Clause, the insurance in favour of the bank does not cease by operation of Condition 3 (alteration of risk), except where
o: The bank has more than one mortgagor on the same property
The property is insured under more than one policy
The breach of the condition has been committed by the bank or its authorised agents
The insured fails to pay premium in advance
e: Clause (v): the bank's interest is protected notwithstanding Condition 3 unless the breach is committed by the bank itself; the bank must notify the insurer of any increase of hazard as soon as it comes to its knowledge.

t: An SFSP policy with sum insured ₹3,000 crore at a location suffers a loss of ₹8 crore. The minimum deductible is
e: SI above ₹2,500 crore per location: 5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹50 lakh; 5% of ₹8 crore = ₹40 lakh, so the minimum of ₹50 lakh applies.

t: A corporate agent may tie up with a maximum of how many insurers in each line of business?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Raised from 3 to 9 insurers per category (life, general, health) by the 2022 amendment to the Corporate Agents Regulations.

t: For an EAR policy with sum insured ₹8 crore, the maximum TPL cover that can be granted is
e: For project SI up to ₹10 crore, TPL may be granted up to ₹1 crore; above ₹10 crore it is 10% of completely erected value or ₹10 crore, whichever is lower.

t: A business has departments A, B and C with turnovers 100, 100 and 50 before loss. After a fire in A, turnovers are 50, 125 and 75 (total unchanged). With the Departmental Clause, the loss of turnover for the claim is
o: Nil, since total turnover is unchanged
100, the full turnover of department A
50, since the results of each department affected are considered separately
25, the net of increases and decreases
e: Departmental clause: the reduction in turnover and ICW provisions apply separately to each affected department; without the clause the claim would be nil as total turnover was maintained.

t: Which of the following policies is normally not issued for a period exceeding 12 months?
e: CPM, MBD, EEI, BPP and DOS are annual (or short-period) policies; project policies (CAR, EAR, MCE) run for the project duration which may exceed 12 months.

t: Stocks of a trader lie in four godowns in different parts of a city, the applicable rates being 1.00‰, 1.20‰, 1.50‰ and 2.00‰. The rate for a floater policy covering all four is
e: Floater rating: the highest rate applicable at any location plus 10% loading = 2.00‰ × 1.10 = 2.20‰.

t: Stock of ₹4 lakh is covered by an SFSP policy for ₹1 lakh and a declaration policy for ₹2 lakh. A loss of ₹3 lakh occurs. The declaration policy pays
e: The SFSP pays 3 × 1/4 = ₹0.75 lakh. The excess of stock value over the SFSP SI is ₹3 lakh, which exceeds the declaration SI, so the SI is used: 3 × 2/4 = ₹1.5 lakh; total ₹2.25 lakh.

t: A 3-year-old wire rope of a crane is replaced in an MBD claim at a cost of ₹2,00,000. The amount payable before excess is
e: Ropes in lifts, cranes and ropeways attract depreciation of 15% per year subject to a maximum of 75%: 3 × 15% = 45%, so 2,00,000 × 55% = ₹1,10,000.

t: Section 3 (Increased Cost of Working) of an Electronic Equipment Insurance policy covers
o: Repair cost of the damaged equipment
Cost of replacing damaged external data media
Cost of hiring substitute equipment, personnel expenses and transportation of materials
Cost of regenerating lost data from back-up
e: EEI has three sections: I material damage, II external data media (replacement of media and data from back-up), III increased cost of working (substitute equipment, personnel, transport).

t: An IAR policy insured's loss is ₹50 lakh and under-insurance is found to be 12%. The under-insurance deduction is
o: Nil, as under-insurance up to 15% is waived
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). IAR special condition: under-insurance up to 15% is waived; if it exceeds 15%, the full under-insurance is applied.

t: Machinery insured under CPM for an individual value of ₹8 lakh is damaged by flood. The claim is ₹1,00,000. The excess applicable is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). CPM AOG excess for individual value over ₹5 lakh up to ₹10 lakh: 3% of SI subject to a minimum of ₹25,000; 3% of ₹8 lakh = ₹24,000, so the minimum ₹25,000 applies.

t: A seasonal godown is insured for 3 months. Sum insured ₹50 lakh, annual rate ₹2.00‰. The premium is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Annual premium = 50,00,000 × 2/1000 = ₹10,000; for a period not exceeding 3 months the short-period scale is 40%, so ₹4,000.

t: For health insurance, the maximum time an insurer may take to decide a cashless authorisation request under the 2024 master circular is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Cashless authorisation within 1 hour of request; final discharge authorisation within 3 hours.

t: The maximum waiting period for pre-existing diseases in health insurance, after the 2024 IRDAI changes, is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Reduced from 48 to 36 months; the moratorium period after which claims cannot be contested (except fraud) is 60 months.

t: A cold storage without FOES extension suffers a compressor breakdown and stock deteriorates. The claim is assessed at ₹2,00,000. The excess applicable is
o: 20% of the claim amount subject to a minimum of ₹20,000
Nil, since there is no FOES extension
e: DOS excess: 20% of claim subject to minimum ₹20,000 (with an 8-hour time excess) for cold storages with FOES extension; 10% of claim amount for those without.

t: An annual SFSP policy (premium ₹12,000) is cancelled at the insured's request after exactly 4 months. The refund due is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Cancellation at the insured's option: premium retained at the short-period scale – 50% for 4 months = ₹6,000 retained, so ₹6,000 refunded.

t: With effect from 1 April 2021, which risks continue to be governed by the erstwhile AIFT 2001?
o: Risks (other than dwellings) where the total value at risk exceeds ₹50 crore at any one location
All risks with sum insured up to ₹5 crore
All dwellings irrespective of sum insured
e: IRDAI notification of 28 December 2020 de-notified the AIFT for dwellings (any SI) and other risks up to ₹50 crore per location from 1 April 2021; larger risks continue under AIFT until further notification.

t: In a life insurance contract, insurable interest must exist:
o: At the time of the claim only
Both at inception and at claim
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Life: at inception only. Marine: at the time of loss. Fire and motor: at both inception and loss.

t: Within how many days of a loss must the insured deliver a written claim with particulars under Condition 6 of the SFSP policy?
e: Condition 6(i): notice of loss forthwith, and within 15 days (or such further time as the insurer allows in writing) a written claim with particulars and details of other insurances.

t: Under the IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests) Regulations 2024, the free-look period for a policy with a term of one year or more is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). 30 days from receipt of the policy document, irrespective of the sales channel.

t: A defective part (A) damages the machine it is fitted in (B), a connected machine (C) and surrounding property (D). Under DE4 cover, what is payable?
e: DE4 excludes only the defective component and access costs; the machine containing it (B), connected machine (C) and surrounding property (D) are payable.

t: The policy wording of the Standard Fire and Special Perils policy appears in which section of AIFT 2001?
e: AIFT: Section I general rules and regulations; Section II policy wording; Sections III–VII rating; Section VIII add-on covers.

t: An EAR proposal is received on 15 May, but the first consignment reached site on 1 May. The premium rate is charged
o: From the date of beginning of erection
From the date of payment of premium
From the date the proposal was received
For the total project period commencing from the date of arrival of the first consignment
e: Rating is for the entire project period from arrival of the first consignment/commencement of work; the insurer is not liable for damage that occurred before the commencement of insurance.

t: A factory rateable under Section IV stops all manufacturing and storage activity continuously for 45 days. The premium retention for the silent period is
o: The appropriate storage rate or the silent risk rate of ₹1.00‰, whichever is higher
Nil, as the risk is silent
e: AIFT Rule 19: silent risk = no manufacturing/storage for 30 days or more; retention at storage rate or ₹1.00‰ whichever is higher; silent rates not allowed after a loss and no discounts apply.
